title: Sara Bensalem 100-Point Spatial Portfolio Audit Rubric
author: Sara Bensalem <sara@sarabensalem.com>

criteria.desc: Project passport clarity (role, tools, client/studio, year)
Problem-solution clarity and spatial concept definition
Scannable typography and concise metadata blocks
First-spread visual hook and editorial rhythm
Scaled architectural plans (1:20 to 1:100) with proper lineweights
Wall sections with layered constructive callouts (waterproofing, insulation, anchors)
Legible dimension chains, floor levels (NGF/TN), and graphic scale bars
Demonstrated knowledge of building codes, PMR/ADA accessibility, and MEP coordination
Consistent multi-column margin and baseline grid across all spreads
Disciplined type hierarchy (max 2 font families, 3 weight variations)
Generous white space (at least 30-35% negative space) avoiding claustrophobic clutter
Alternating rhythm between full-bleed hero spreads and dense technical sets
Macro urban context, site plan, topography contours, or transit networks
Meso architectural building volumes, massing diagrams, and internal circulation
Micro interior joinery, bespoke furniture prototype, or tectonic joint detail
Tactile material triptych, texture swatches, and physical sample boards
Deliberate lighting scenography (day/night comparison, natural filtration, artificial fixtures)
Sophisticated, grounded color palette (warm greiges, muted earth tones, noble stone minerals)
Optimized binary PDF (< 50 MB) with clean vector linework and sharp text layers
Real-world validation (on-site construction supervision, built client commissions, competition laurels)
Professional CV, toolchain matrix, and clean contact colophon
